entry.title: A Box of 23 Cardboard-Loving Cat Memes That Fit & Sit in Your Heart
entry.summary: Cats never miss an opportunity to jump into every space, no matter its size or availability status. I don't need to iterate on how cats enter every cardboard box they see, or literally any other small space they locate. But first - why do they even do that? In short, cats simply feel safe inside. Having an enclosed space around them, like a cardboard box, gives them a sense of security - however real or not. They also view these spaces as strategic vantage points to pounce on prey from - so basically a place to cosplay big cats. So basically it's just another proof that cats make no sense at all. Their logic is not logicing. But this is why we love them so much. My cat found herself in the most ridiculous situations because of this internal drive she has to enter literally anywhere. To do the fits and sits even if she doesn't fit and cannot sit. She once got herself stuck behind the washing machine because she absolutely insisted this nook must be explored - she just had no idea how to get herself out. At another time, she got locked inside the pots and pans cabinet, which is protected by a child lock. It was open for one second, and she still managed to get herself inside. But all of that doesn't make her experience with classic cardboard boxes any easier. That child lock I've mentioned? It's there for a reason. The reason being a 1-year-old roaming free in the house because she's been walking since she was 10 months old. That kid sees the cat entering a cardboard box I left on the floor for her and thinks, "I'm going to get inside to cuddle the cat." My cat bolts away every single time. Raising cats and kids together is not a simple task. But cats will always cat, and that means they'll fit, sit, and be absolutely smug about it. And honestly? It makes them even more special than they already are.

entry.title: Strict vegan adopts very first kitten, then realizes that her tiny carnivore needs meat for life, and cat owners have a tough message for her: 'Their wellbeing comes first'
entry.summary: What happens when our purrsonal ethics conflict with the biological needs of an animal we chose to care for? There are a lot of things about cat ownership that become so normal you quickly furrget how objectively weird they are. You scoop their bathroom business into a plastic bag multiple times per day, you spend money on furniture specifically designed to be destroyed, and you quickly learn the difference between their different kinds of meows. One can mean "I'm hungry" and another can mean "I saw a bug a few hours ago and you must know about it." You fellow cat pawrents know what I'm talking about. And then there is feeding them meat. I don't think anyone likes it. All the wet foods have this weird smell that, even after 12 years of owning cats, I still can't get over. Don't even get me started on the ingredients. Most longtime cat pawrents probably do not think very deeply about it every time they crack open a can. Cats eat meat, that is simply part of the deal. For one brand-new kitten owner, though, that realization caused something of a moral meat crisis. They eagerly went out and bought them high-quality kitten food while focusing on giving their baby the best pawssible start. Then, as a strict vegan, they realized that every can of cat food represented an ethical equation they had spent years trying to remove themselves from. Smartly, they did want to force their beliefs onto their kitten, but they also wondered whether there was another way to make it work. And this is where I think the story gets really interesting, because this is something a lot of vegans deal with. And, we all know that people have a lot of feelings about veganism, whether it's for or against.

entry.title: Person adopts the most terrified kitten in the shelter, and after months of careful trustbuilding, she finally lets herself be petted and purrs: '[She was] trying to make herself as small as possible'
entry.summary: With shy cats, patience pays off more than anything else. We, as humans, have a certain understanding of what love looks like. And whether we do it on purpose or not, we apply that understanding to our cats as well. Now, with dogs, it's simpler. Their way of showing affection is very obvious, it's very in your face. With cats, it's not quite that easy. Some cats are total velcro cats. They are all about physical contact. They will cuddle with you and climb up on you, and if you don't pet them at least 116 times a day, they will riot and directly on your face. But most cats are not like that. Cats have their own love language. Cats show affection by slowly blinking at you. They show affection by turning their back on you, by sleeping next to you, by spending long stretches of time in the same room as you. And we know- that's not the same as cuddling your cat. Of course it's not. But their expression of love is no less valid than yours. And then, there are shy cats. And shy cats, ones who are a little scared of humans, a little wary of letting their guard down, they show affection in their own ways as well. They do it in small ways, slowly warming up to you. We can't tell you the exact way. It's up to you to pay attention to them and learn how they show love. And you have to appreciate those little things just as much as you would a cuddle session. Maybe once you do that, once they feel comfortable enough with you, they will learn a little about your love language as well.

entry.title: 20 Cats Being Furry Friends and Embracing Feline Friendliness
entry.summary: How we begin our morning may dictate how the rest of the day goes, so starting on the right paw with these friendly cat memes may just do the trick! Being a cat pawrent can be summed up pretty easily. You wake up a pink nose in your face, the breath of a cat's mouth inhaling and exhaling right on top of you, and a few licks to your cheeks before you pull yourself from the sweet slumber you were in to feed this hungry kitty. You wake up to the cheer, smile, and morning barks of joy from your little one. They may not always seem like it but they're full of friendly friendship despite their chaotic appearance and behavior. One second they're peacefully napping, paws twitching in dreamland, and the next, they're sitting upright and giving you a look that makes you question whether you're safe to fall asleep tonight. Their eyes are shining in hope that you'll give them what they want. And if they hear the crinkle of the treat bag, be prepared to give them something, because they won't stop until they have it. They might even sneak up behind you for something you're already eating, as we all know the hungry appetite of a cat. Heaven forbid you sit down for a bite without inviting them, or giving them a piece of what you're eating. They will throw their paws right on the table if they have to just for a bit of your bite. And there you have it! The world of cat pawrenting. But never fear, because all the hostility is simply on the surface of what's actually going on, and what's underneath is furry friendship, and cats that embrace feline friendliness. We all need a friend in the world, and cats are no different. So if you're wondering why your cat acts so hot and cold to you, remember that they indeed love and need you, but they sometimes need to give the cold shoulder too. At the end of the day, they're still cats. And their love is expressed through the looks of anger, terror, or mischief.

entry.title: Couple rescues terrified kitten from neighboring building, and she attaches herself to the woman asking for constant cuddles and uppies: ‘She trusts me 100%’
entry.summary: Have you ever had a cat with attachment issues? Cats are not usually very clingy, but sometimes they choose their hoomans as their safe space. When an animal has been abandoned, it's usual for them to have trust issues in relation to human beings. After all, they were the ones who abandoned them in the first place. Both cats and dogs alike can be scared, reluctant to trust and jumpy before any kind of strange noise. I've seen rescued cats and dogs behaving in the same way. The first week my kitty was at home after she was rescued, she was terrified. She opened her eyes round and wide as two full moons; her ears were always up, and she turned her head form one side to the other. All she did was cuddle in the couch and sleep, and every time someone made the smallest of noises, she would run away and hide under the couch. We couldn't even open the front door without her getting scared and hiding. It took her a few weeks to get used to the sounds of the house, and even months to start trusting us an behaving like a regular cat. She wouldn't meow at first either! She was so silent, as if she was afraid thta, if we noticed she was there, we would hurt her. It breaks my heart to remember it, but luckily, now she's all better. Now, she meows normally, although she's not the most talkative. She always gets the zoomies, and plays around the house. She's even starting to misbehave! Now, I can't stop her from scratching the furniture or jumping all over the dining table. Seriously, if anyone has the number of a good cat trainer, please, send it to me. I'm getting desperate, and now I can't get her to quit her bad habits. In this case, this couple rescued a girl cat who was terrified, and in bringing her to their home, she chose the woman as her source of protection. Now, she won't leave her alone, and she follows her everywhere.

entry.title: ‘The Cat Distribution System chose my yard 3 times’: Woman’s five-cat household grows to eight over two years, and every new arrival opens the family's heart a little more
entry.summary: Watching the Cat Distribution System work its magic is like looking at the most heartwarming magic show in the world. Nobody knows how the Cat Distribution System actually works. Not even we here at the I Can Has Cheezburger HQ. But they (it?) have three parts to their name, so I'll try my best to explore and explain what the CDS actually is in three parts - just like the three cats it sent to this one woman below. Firstly, cat. When you talk about the CDS, you talk about cats. There are plenty of cats in need out there on the streets - some are hungry, others are suffering extreme weather conditions, and other cats deal with all of these while also giving birth to kittens outside. That's a crazy thought to hold, especially if you're a cat lover. For me at least, it's hard thinking there are cats outside right now that might need help that I can't give them at the moment. It breaks my heart a little. Secondly, distribution. The CDS doesn't just deal with cats - it sends them where they need to go. Or, you know, it distributes them. Somewhere out there, there's a human who will give a cat a forever home, and that might just be this specific human and that specific cat. And that distribution part is what makes this matchmaking take place. But how do they know to match the right cat to the right person, and vice versa? That's where the third part comes in, the system. It's not random, despite it being seen as such. Take this one woman who tells her CDS story below - it seems like such a coincidence that she'd be chosen for a match three times, but that's not a random chance at all. This is the CDS at work. You see, she already had five cats, which immediately flagged her as a safe space for cats on the CDS side. They didn't wander into her yard "just because" - they went there to meet their forever home. It's exactly where and when they should've been.

entry.title: A Warm Mug of 31 Steaming Hot Cat Memes For Slow Morning Scrolling
entry.summary: Everyone loves the feeling of holding a big, warm mug in their hands. Why not fill it with cat memes? Ahhh, the ineffable feeling of a warm mug in your hands juxtaposed with the cold, brisk winter weather outside. There's nothing cozier than balancing the cold air with something warm. Whether that thing is a mug of hot cocoa to start your day, coffee, snuggling your favorite person, cat, or dog, or whether it's scrolling cat memes is entirely up to you. When you know what self soothes you, you know you can always help yourself. The great thing about cat memes is that you can do it anytime, anywhere, and with anyone. The warmth of their kookiness, the comedy of their capricious chaos, and the pawdorable big innocent eyes they give us are all ways to find our center. In the morning, our brains are fragile. Our consciousness teeming with tasks for the day, to-do lists, errands, and responsibilities. Reality begins to obfuscate itself with urgency and expectation. Cat memes, however, cut through that fog. They don't clarify your problems, but they make them feel less urgent. They remind you that even the most confident creature can wake up confused, disheveled, and mildly offended by daylight. Slow morning scrolling is never something to be ashamed of. These steaming hot memes act as a buffer between sleep and society. Each swipe is a small pause, a chance to smile before the noise ramps up. A cat stretched across a keyboard. A kitten mid-yawn, mouth impossibly wide. A face that perfectly captures how it feels to be awake but not emotionally available yet.

entry.title: Cute and Curious Cats Popping Out of Pumpkins for a Pawsitively Purrecious Halloween
entry.summary: It's pumpkin season, and cats are getting in on the fun! While the rest of us are busy decorating our homes for Halloween, some curious kitties have discovered that pumpkins make pretty great places to hang out. We have to say, they're making a strong case for being the cutest Halloween decorations around. Cats have always had a thing for climbing inside anything they can fit into. Leave an empty cardboard box on the floor, and your kitty will probably be sitting in it before you've finished unpacking. Laundry baskets, shopping bags, and bathroom sinks are all fair game, too. So it makes sense that a hollowed-out pumpkin would catch their attention. It's basically a seasonal cat bed, although we're not sure how comfortable it actually is. There's just so much to love about a little feline face peeking out of a pumpkin. The tiny ears, the curious eyes, and those whiskers sticking out over the edge make for an adorable sight. Some kittens are small enough to fit their entire bodies inside, while bigger cats have to settle for poking their heads through the opening. Either way, we wouldn't mind having a few of these little pumpkin dwellers decorating our homes. We have to give some credit to the hoomans who manage to capture these moments on camera. Anyone who's tried photographing a cat knows that getting them to cooperate isn't always easy. You can have everything set up perfectly, only for your kitty to decide that the pumpkin is much more interesting from the outside. Maybe they'll give it a sniff, bat at the stem, or wander off before you can take a single picture. Even when a cat does decide to climb inside, there's no guarantee they'll stay there long enough for a photoshoot. One second, they're sitting sweetly in their little pumpkin house, and the next, they're climbing out because they've spotted a leaf blowing across the yard. We can't blame them for being curious, but we'd definitely appreciate a few extra seconds to get the camera focused! Pumpkins are cute, but pumpkins with whiskers are even better!

entry.title: The Story Behind Amsterdam's Floating Cat Shelter, Where Rescued Cats Find a Home on the Water
entry.summary: How did I visit Amsterdam and miss a boat full of rescued stray cats??? I wish I'd known about De Poezenboot sooner. The name means Catboat and refers to Amsterdam's floating cat shelter. The owners describe it as the only floating cat sanctuary in the world. Now my question is: why are we tourists visiting the Van Gogh Museum and not this shelter? I would have gone straight there if I knew about it. The works of art are of a different kind, but still, I bet tourists walk out of the place equally astonished by the cuteness. According to its official history, it all started back in 1966 when a woman named Henriette van Weelde found a mother cat and her kittens beneath a tree opposite her home. She took them in, and more cats followed, including animals whose owners could no longer care for them. She was soon recognized as the "cat lady" in the neighborhood. Two years later, she was running out of room for the animals, so she came up with the coolest idea ever: buying a boat for the cats so they could live there. Yes, she bought an old Dutch sailing barge and turned it into a cat shelter. If people can live in boats, why can't cats? Some volunteers joined her, and the Catboat Foundation became official.
